label: Early copy steps (outputs 1-3) of length-9 sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost only in the longest sequences (L=9 holds 94% of activation mass, L=8 about 6%, L<=7 almost none). Within those it fires on copy steps outputting original tokens 1-3 (t=10-12 for L=9), peaking at recall_idx 2, which is the step right after the first copied token is fed back (prev2_tok=<DEL>). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, or on the first occurrence of a token. A small secondary bump sits on the last one or two copy steps of L=9 sequences (about 3% of mass). The predicate captures about 90% of activation mass, but precision is low (about 0.22) because only around a fifth of eligible steps fire. Whether it fires and how strongly depends on token identity: inputs f, d, b, 0, w, r give the highest rates, and the strongest activations are at recall_idx 2 when the fed-back input is orig(1) = f/b/0. Token-set filters raise precision but cost too much recall to produce a clean rule.
